title: Russia moves HUGE stash of new tanks to Nato border but if Putin invades his men will be massacred!
summary: A retired British officer on reports of Russia rebuilding tanks near Finland, Norway and the Baltic states, and why an armoured attack would fail for now.

assertions.quote: it is very clear that Russia is on a war economy, on a war setting.

verdicts.note: Russian defence spending is around 6-7 percent of GDP and open-source counts show large refurbishment and new T-90M output.

DDIS says Russia's defence industry has produced more equipment and ammunition than the war consumes since 2024 and out-produces Europe's, but gives no tank figures and expects output hard to raise beyond 2025 levels.

assertions.quote: Predominantly, uh up very north of Russia, close to the Finnish border and the Norwegian border as well.

verdicts.note: Based on one newspaper's imagery report, not independently confirmed.

DDIS reports Russia has deployed new army units along the Finnish border and behind the Baltic states, with far more troops expected after the war, but says the Ukraine war is delaying this build-up and does not mention armour stockpiles.

assertions.quote: an armored thrust with purely tanks and BMPs against the Baltic states or or Finland, I I expect they they would get absolutely massacred

verdicts.note: Against NATO air power it would likely take heavy losses, but wargames such as RAND's show Russia could still reach Baltic capitals quickly.

assertions.quote: to get on the offensive, to take and hold ground, you still need tanks and armor supported by drones.

verdicts.note: Ukraine shows drones blunt armour while combined drone and armour attacks have retaken some ground; the balance is still shifting.

assertions.quote: doing a whole host of activity, the hybrid war against the West and against the UK in particular

verdicts.note: European governments attribute a wave of sabotage, arson and drone incursions, including the September 2025 drone incursion into Poland, to Russia.

assertions.quote: we need a deterrence uh supporting Finland and Norway and the Baltic states to make sure that when Putin looks at them

verdicts.note: EFIS credits steps taken by Estonia and Europe with making the Kremlin calculate carefully and says firm, steady preparedness is what truly deters Russia.
